failureDomains: FD1: Beijing production plus short-RPO local operational staging
FD2: cross-region object storage under a separate backup writer identity, with versioning and Object Lock/WORM compliance retention
FD3: Phoenix or another independent provider for encrypted secondary recovery copies; ordinary ext4 is not immutable
targetArchitecture.minimumAcceptance: FD1 plus FD2 is mandatory; FD3 is strongly recommended and must not share provider, account root, or deletion authority with FD2.
targetArchitecture.objectLock: Create a new bucket with Object Lock enabled at creation, use compliance mode for committed generations, deny retention bypass and lifecycle shortening to the backup writer, and keep break-glass administration separate.
targetArchitecture.encryption: Encrypt each package client-side with an envelope key before transfer; keep the KEK in a separately administered KMS or offline recovery escrow; provider-side encryption is defense in depth, not the sole control.
targetArchitecture.integrity: Retain backup.mjs manifest.json, SHA-256 and byte length for every member; add a signed package/index digest; verify upload checksum and later download checksum against the signed index.
targetArchitecture.retention: Suggested baseline: 35 daily, 13 weekly and 12 monthly generations; WORM compliance retention at least 90 days, with monthly generations retained 365 days. Legal and privacy review must approve before implementation.
targetArchitecture.restoreDrill: Weekly manifest/integrity verification and monthly isolated restore on a non-production host; quarterly sampled recovery from the WORM target using a fresh destination, SQLite quick_check, semantic validation and a read-only user journey.
targetArchitecture.rpoRtoProposal: RPO 24 hours for immutable offsite copies; RTO 8 hours for declared regional loss, pending measured drill evidence.

implementationGates: Human approval of providers, regions, cost, retention and data residency.
Creation/configuration of storage, Object Lock, KMS and identities under a separately authorized change.
A credential-minimized writer path that cannot delete versions, shorten retention or administer keys.
One synthetic-data end-to-end upload/download/restore drill before any production-data transfer.
A separately approved first production transfer with monitoring, checksum evidence and egress/cost limits.

failureAndRollbackBoundary.beforeFirstTransfer: Abandon the candidate configuration; no production state changes are required.
failureAndRollbackBoundary.partialUpload: Do not publish the generation index; leave or lifecycle the incomplete object only under an approved storage policy.
failureAndRollbackBoundary.checksumOrRestoreFailure: Quarantine the generation, preserve evidence, keep the prior accepted generation, and do not alter live production.
failureAndRollbackBoundary.objectLockMisconfiguration: Stop the backup pipeline. Compliance-locked objects cannot be shortened or deleted; rollback means selecting a corrected new bucket/generation, not mutating retained objects.
failureAndRollbackBoundary.keyLoss: Treat the copy as unrecoverable; preserve other domains and rotate to a newly approved envelope key. Never test key rotation first on the only accepted generation.
